description: Close the cam runtime-artifact ignore gap in the repo's own .gitignore and bring templates/.gitignore to derived parity, locked by a derived parity script and durable behavioral tests

officialDocsConsulted.summary: Documented exit codes are 0 (ignored), 1 (not ignored), 128 (fatal error), confirming GOTCHA 2's rule that any code above 1 is an error and never a verdict. Critical additional finding: by default tracked files are NOT reported at all ('they are not subject to exclude rules'), so a negative control run inside this repo against a TRACKED path returns 1 regardless of the ignore rules and is vacuous unless --no-index is passed; verified empirically (tracked path plus blanket rule: default exit 1, --no-index exit 0). Paths need not exist on disk for check-ignore to evaluate them.
officialDocsConsulted.localConventionConflict: The issue-mandated parity script (GOTCHA 1) probes in default mode, where tracked-by-design state paths always report 'not ignored' on the repo side; that is the form the operator already swept red/green, so it stays verbatim, while the repo-side negative control in US-001 must use --no-index to be falsifiable.

userStories.title: Ignore the three uncovered cam runtime artifacts in the repo's own .gitignore
userStories.description: As the maintainer of this public repo, whose agents run with bypassPermissions and are instructed to commit every change, I need the repo's own .gitignore to ignore the three cam runtime artifacts that escape today, so a background watcher's full stdout/stderr log, its pid file and the merge-watch state cannot be committed and pushed by an autonomous worker.
acceptanceCriteria: The repo's own .gitignore makes git ignore .claude/cam-sidecar-liveness-watcher.log, .claude/.cam-sidecar-liveness-watcher.pid and .claude/.cam-merge-watch.json (issue AC1; the command prints NOT IGNORED for all three and exits 1 on unmodified main). [oracle: for p in .claude/cam-sidecar-liveness-watcher.log .claude/.cam-sidecar-liveness-watcher.pid .claude/.cam-merge-watch.json; do git check-ignore -q "$p" || { echo "NOT IGNORED $p"; exit 1; }; done; echo OK]

The three new rules are per-artifact, never a blanket: with them in place two durable tracked paths stay unignored, checked with --no-index so a tracked path is really evaluated against the rules, and with any exit code above 1 treated as an error rather than as a verdict. This is an invariance pin (green on main by design); its falsifiability is exercised by the blanket-substitution mutation in US-003. [oracle: for p in .claude/agents/subagent-planner.md scripts/cam/patterns.md; do git check-ignore --no-index -q "$p"; rc=$?; case "$rc" in 1) ;; *) echo "UNEXPECTED $p rc=$rc"; exit 1;; esac; done; echo OK]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
userStories.notes: Single file: .gitignore at the repo root. Add the three rules next to the existing runtime-marker block, each as a precise per-artifact line with a CAM-502 comment tag, following the shape already used for .claude/cam-recycle-watcher.log and the durable markers. Writers, for the comment provenance: .claude/cam-sidecar-liveness-watcher.log is written by the watcher spawn in src/commands/run.ts:1142; .cam-sidecar-liveness-watcher.pid by SIDECAR_LIVENESS_WATCHER_PID_FILE in src/supervisor/sidecar-pid.ts:189; .cam-merge-watch.json by MERGE_WATCH_FILENAME in src/release/merge-watch.ts:40. SCOPE: this story touches only the repo's own .gitignore; templates/.gitignore is owned by US-002 and will legitimately change later on this same branch, so do not add any branch-scoped 'templates untouched' assertion. GOTCHA (git docs, this PRD's officialDocsConsulted): git check-ignore exits 0 ignored, 1 not ignored, 128 fatal; when hand-running any probe, an exit code above 1 is an ERROR and must never be read as 'not ignored', and a probe against a TRACKED path is suppressed (always 1) unless --no-index is passed, which is why the negative-control oracle here carries --no-index. No templates/ or vendor/ change here, so no embed-vendor step. patterns.md context: the CAM-499 bullet on .env.*.local glob semantics (a * matches zero-or-more chars but the literal dots must still be present) is the nearest precedent for getting a rule shape right on the first pass.

userStories.title: Add the derived parity check script and bring templates/.gitignore to parity
userStories.description: As the operator of a gship-init-ed project, I need the .gitignore that gship init installs to ignore exactly the same cam runtime artifacts the cam-cli repo ignores, enforced by an oracle derived live from src/ rather than by a hand-grown list, so my project stops committing the event log, supervisor log and durable markers alongside my code, and so the eighth hand-enumerated recurrence cannot happen.
acceptanceCriteria: scripts/check-gitignore-parity.sh exists, derives its probe set live by grepping src, index.ts and scripts/*.ts (the GOTCHA 1 derivation, verbatim), compares the git check-ignore verdict of every probe under templates/.gitignore materialized in a throwaway git repo against the verdict under the repo's own .gitignore, and exits 0 with no DIVERGE line for this repo (unmodified main prints 13 DIVERGE lines; before this story the script does not exist and the command fails). [oracle: bash scripts/check-gitignore-parity.sh .]

The check is non-vacuous: it prints the derived probe count on its own line as PROBES=<n> before comparing anything (issue AC6; measured 42 on main today). [oracle: bash scripts/check-gitignore-parity.sh . | grep -qE '^PROBES=([3-9][0-9]|[0-9]{3,})$']

The check fails closed when the derivation degenerates: run against a throwaway git repo that holds only a copy of templates/.gitignore and has no src/ to derive from, it must FAIL rather than pass on an empty probe set (issue AC6; expressed as negation of the command, never as a comparison against a literal exit code). [oracle: T=$(mktemp -d); git init -q "$T"; mkdir -p "$T/templates"; cp templates/.gitignore "$T/templates/.gitignore"; test -f scripts/check-gitignore-parity.sh && ! bash "$(pwd)/scripts/check-gitignore-parity.sh" "$T"]

Anti-regression of the oracle itself (issue AC4): the check contains no artifact name written by hand outside the derivation pattern, so it cannot silently decay back into an enumerated list. [oracle: test -f scripts/check-gitignore-parity.sh && ! grep -qE 'cam-worker-events|cam-supervisor\.log|cam-gate-history|cam-merge-watch|liveness-watcher' scripts/check-gitignore-parity.sh]

The script's header comment states the limitation of the oracle in these terms: it is a set-equality comparison between the two files, so it detects DIVERGENCE only and stays green for an artifact that is ignored by NEITHER file (the class US-001 had to fix by hand); the header names the coverage sweep as the complementary check. [oracle: grep -q 'set-equality' scripts/check-gitignore-parity.sh]

templates/.gitignore is brought to parity and the embedded copy is regenerated in the same commit, so what gship init actually ships carries the new rules (issue AC5). [oracle: bun run embed-vendor:check]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
userStories.notes: Files: scripts/check-gitignore-parity.sh (new), templates/.gitignore, src/vendor/_generated.ts (regenerated, never hand-edited: run bun run embed-vendor). Copy the GOTCHA 1 body from the issue VERBATIM (it was already swept red on main with 13 divergences, green under the positive control, and red in both directions under substitution mutation); the only additions are the PROBES=<n> line and the fail-closed guard on an empty probe set. Do not reinvent the derivation and do not add --no-index to it: in default mode a tracked path is reported as not-ignored on the repo side, and that is the semantics the operator's sweep baselined; changing it would invalidate the swept result. After US-001, the 16 rules the template needs are the 13 DIVERGE lines on main (.claude/.cam-gate.json, .cam-implement-blocked.json, .cam-orch-session, .cam-plan-preflight-failed.json, .cam-post-merge-stalled.json, .cam-ship-stalled.json, .cam-sidecar-session.json, .cam-supervisor.lock, .cam-worker-pane, cam-gate-history.jsonl, cam-supervisor.log, cam-worker-events.jsonl, plus root gate-results.json) and the three from US-001; derive the exact list by running the script rather than by transcribing this note. Set-equality also fails if the template ignores something the repo does not, which is what keeps the CAM-27 tracked-by-design state files honest for free, with no exception list. WHY BASH, and the trade-off (recorded deliberately): the issue mandates this exact already-swept shell oracle, git check-ignore probing is native to shell, and scripts/build-release.sh is the in-repo precedent for a .sh; the cost is that a .sh gets no biome lint, no knip and no type coverage, so US-004 buys that coverage back by driving this script from a real bun test (which the existing check:all `test` gate already runs in CI) instead of registering a new entry in the GATES manifest in scripts/check-all.ts, which would otherwise be the only gate in that manifest with no static coverage at all. Keep the script small enough to stay under the file-size budget (scripts/cam/file-size-budget.json) without a raise.

userStories.title: Durable behavioral test that the shipped template ignores every cam runtime artifact
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I need a durable test that drives real git check-ignore against the .gitignore produced by materializeTemplates (the EMBEDDED copy the product actually ships), on both materialization paths and with negative controls in both blanket directions, so the parity fixed by US-002 cannot regress silently and cannot be faked by a blanket rule.
acceptanceCriteria: test/templates-gitignore-runtime-artifacts.test.ts exercises real git check-ignore in a fresh tmpdir git repo over the .gitignore produced by materializeTemplates, asserting every cam runtime artifact covered by US-001 and US-002 is ignored, and it covers BOTH production paths of src/templates/embedded.ts: the verbatim-write path (no pre-existing .gitignore) and the non-destructive mergeGitignore path (pre-existing .gitignore). [oracle: bun test test/templates-gitignore-runtime-artifacts.test.ts]

The test carries a negative control in both blanket directions, using durable tracked files: .claude/agents/subagent-planner.md must stay unignored (catches a blanket .claude/*) and scripts/cam/patterns.md must stay unignored (catches a blanket scripts/cam/*), asserted on both materialization paths. [oracle: file-assert grep -q 'subagent-planner.md' test/templates-gitignore-runtime-artifacts.test.ts && grep -q 'scripts/cam/patterns.md' test/templates-gitignore-runtime-artifacts.test.ts]

The test's check-ignore helper treats an exit code above 1 as an error and never as a verdict (GOTCHA 2), so a negative control can never pass for the wrong reason. [oracle: file-assert grep -q 'exitCode > 1' test/templates-gitignore-runtime-artifacts.test.ts]

The falsifiability sweep is actually performed, in BOTH mutation directions, against the file the test really reads: delete precise rules, then substitute them with a blanket, running bun run embed-vendor after each mutation so it lands in src/vendor/_generated.ts, observing the test RED each time, then restoring. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]

scripts/cam/patterns.md gains a bullet recording that sweep, tagged CAM-502, quoting the exact assertion or probe path observed failing under the blanket-substitution mutation. [oracle: file-assert grep -q 'CAM-502' scripts/cam/patterns.md]
Vendor drift check passes (bun run embed-vendor:check), proving the mutation sweep was fully reverted. [oracle: bun run embed-vendor:check]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
userStories.notes: Files: test/templates-gitignore-runtime-artifacts.test.ts (new), scripts/cam/patterns.md. Model the new file on test/templates-gitignore-dotenv.test.ts (CAM-499): same makeTmpRepo + isIgnored + two-path describe shape, but with the strict helper required here (throw when the exit code is above 1 instead of collapsing every non-zero into 'not ignored'). GOTCHA 3, reincident from CAM-499: the test imports materializeTemplates, which reads the copy embedded in src/vendor/_generated.ts, NOT templates/.gitignore on disk; mutating the disk file and seeing the test stay green proves nothing except that the mutation went to the wrong file, so always run bun run embed-vendor before re-running the test during the sweep, and count the target token in the file the test reads. GOTCHA 4 (CAM-495 and CAM-499, twice reincident): deletion mutation does not cover substitution; the blanket direction is exactly what the two negative controls exist to catch. In the tmpdir repo the probe files are untracked, so the plain default check-ignore form is correct there (unlike the repo-side probe in US-001, which needed --no-index for tracked paths). Do NOT target the rotating per-story state files under scripts/cam/ as oracle paths; the tracked-by-design invariant for them is already covered for free by the set-equality parity oracle of US-002. patterns.md precedent to extend, not duplicate: the CAM-499 bullet on a positive-control-only suite passing unchanged under a strictly-broader implementation.

userStories.title: Drive the parity check from bun test so CI enforces it and the bash script gets source-guard coverage
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I need the derived parity check executed by the test suite, so the template-vs-repo ignore parity is re-verified by the existing CI test gate on every change instead of depending on someone remembering to run a shell script, and so the one non-TypeScript check in this repo still has a guard pinning its derivation shape and its fail-closed behaviour.
acceptanceCriteria: test/check-gitignore-parity-script.test.ts runs the real scripts/check-gitignore-parity.sh as a subprocess against the repo root and asserts a zero exit with no DIVERGE line in its stdout, so the parity is enforced by bun test (and therefore by the existing check:all test gate in CI) rather than by a manual run. [oracle: bun test test/check-gitignore-parity-script.test.ts]

The same test pins the non-vacuity leg by asserting the PROBES line in the script's stdout is above the degeneracy floor, so an empty or collapsed derivation can never read as a pass. [oracle: file-assert grep -q 'PROBES=' test/check-gitignore-parity-script.test.ts]

The same test pins the source-guard leg by asserting the script text carries no hand-written artifact literal (issue AC4), so the derivation cannot be quietly replaced with an enumerated list in a later edit. [oracle: file-assert grep -q 'cam-worker-events' test/check-gitignore-parity-script.test.ts]

The same test covers the fail-closed leg: the script run against a throwaway repo that holds only a copy of templates/.gitignore and no src/ exits non-zero, with any subprocess failure distinguished from a legitimate verdict. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]

The falsifiability sweep is performed: with templates/.gitignore mutated on disk (first by removing one precise rule, then by substituting a blanket), this test is observed RED both times and green again after restore. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]
Vendor drift check passes (bun run embed-vendor:check), proving the disk mutations of the sweep were fully reverted. [oracle: bun run embed-vendor:check]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
userStories.notes: Single new file: test/check-gitignore-parity-script.test.ts. This story is the compensating coverage recorded in US-002's notes for choosing a .sh: the precedent is test/build-release-smoke.test.ts, which guards the repo's other shell script. DELIBERATELY OUT OF SCOPE: do not add a new entry to the GATES manifest in scripts/check-all.ts. Every gate there is a bun-run TypeScript script, a bash gate would be the only one with no lint, no knip and no unit coverage, and no issue acceptance criterion asks for a new gate; running the script from bun test gives the same CI enforcement through the existing test gate. Run the script with Bun.spawnSync(['bash', 'scripts/check-gitignore-parity.sh', repoRoot]) from the repo root (real subprocess, real git, per the repo's test-quality rule of hitting real I/O at wire boundaries), decode stdout once and assert on it; treat a git or bash failure code above the script's own contract as an error, never as a verdict. HONEST LIMITATION to keep in mind while writing assertions and any comment: the parity check is a set-equality comparison, so it detects template-vs-repo DIVERGENCE only; an artifact ignored by NEITHER file (the exact class US-001 fixed by hand) produces zero DIVERGE lines and passes. Do not describe this test, in prose or in comments, as closing that class. A universal both-sides assertion is not derivable today, because the probe set legitimately contains tracked-by-design state files and truncated glob prefixes (.claude/.cam-task-prompt-, .claude/.cam-worker-, GOTCHA 5), so it would need exactly the hand-maintained exception list the issue identifies as the root cause.
